items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: We’re trying the same thing with Kenny Peplowski and Johnny Varro and myself.

ctx.x: B.G., yeah. Yeah, he was great, great. He never cared for me, but gez, I heard some fantastic things he’s done. Still, even now, you’ll bring back some old things he did. My wife and I were listening to him on a tape, 1935, 1938 with Gene and Teddy. They had to divide it up and it was much better as a trio, it really was. They could do whatever they wanted you know? They didn’t have to worry about getting the keys right in the middle of a song, just look at Teddy and Teddy looked at him and they knew just what…
How does it change your playing to work without a bass player?
